units: <cite ref="Yoma 75a:21">Yoma 75ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>בשר ששָׁאֲלוּ שלא וכ׳</he> flesh for which they asked unreasonably was given them at an unreasonable time (in the evening) &c.
<cite ref="Taanit 4a:4">Taan. 4ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="E00193"><he>הוֹגָן</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 5:2">Ber. V, 2</cite> (<cite ref="Berakhot 33a:11">33ᵃ</cite>) <he>הגשמים וכ׳</he> (<cite ref="G00078"><he>את</he></cite>) <he>ושׁוֹאֲלִין</he> (Bab. ed. <he>ושְׁאֵלָה</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.) and the prayer for rain is inserted in the Benediction of Years (the ninth section of the Prayer of Benedictions, v. <cite ref="U01570"><he>שָׁנָה</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 1:1">Taan. I, 1</cite> <he>אף אני לא אמרתי לִשְׁאוֹל אלא להזכיר</he> I also did not say, ‘to ask’ for rain, but to mention rain.
<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 1:2">Ib. 2</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:2:8">Y. Ber. V, 9ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>שׁוֹאֵל צרכיו</he>, v. <cite ref="R00255"><he>צוֹרֶךְ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 9:1">B. Bath. IX, 1</cite> <he>יִשְׁאֲלוּ וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="Q02147"><he>פֶּתַח</he></cite>.
Ab. IV, 18 ואל תִּשְׁאַל לו בשעת נדרו ask not thy neighbor (as to circumstances which may change the aspects of his vow) at the moment of his vow, v. infra Nif.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:7">Ib. V, 7</cite> <he>שואל כענין ומשיב וכ׳</he> he (the wise student) asks pertinent questions, and (when asked) replies in agreement with the adopted law.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 36a:14">Bekh. 36ᵃ</cite> <he>עמד השואל וש׳ יכ׳</he> the questioner (at college) arose and asked &c.
<cite ref="Nedarim 20a:14">Ned. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>שָׁאֲלוּ את וכ׳</he> they asked Imma Shalom &c.
<cite ref="Niddah 68b:30">Nidd. 68ᵇ</cite> <he>בראשון לא שָׁאַלְתִּי … שלא שאלתי</he> as to the first day I did not ask, and I made a mistake in not asking.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 68:4">Gen. R. s. 68</cite> <he>מטרונה שָׁאֲלָה וכ׳</he> a Roman matron asked R. José &c.; a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Yoma 73a:19">Yoma 73ᵃ</cite> <he>כיצד שׁוֹאֲלִין השואל פניו כלפי נִשְׁאָל הנשאל וכ׳</he> how were the Urim and Tummim consulted? The inquirer had his face directed to him (the priest) who was consulted, and the latter directed himself to the Divine Presence (the Urim and Tummim).
Ib. אין שואלין שני וכ׳ you must not ask two questions at a time; a. fr.—ש׳ בשלום (or sub. בשלום) to salute.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 21b:11">M. Kat. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>הוא שואל בשלום אחרים … אחרים אין שואלין בשלומו וכ׳</he> he (the mourner during the first thirty days) may inquire after the peace of others, for they dwell in peace, but others must not inquire after his peace, for he does not dwell in peace.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 21b:8">Ib.</cite> <he>משיב ואינו שואל</he>, v. <cite ref="U00311"><he>שׁוּב</he></cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (cmp. דָּרַשׁ) to discuss, lecture. Tosef. Meg. IV (III), 5 שואלין הילכות וכ׳ the laws of Passover are expounded on Passover &c., v. עִנְיָן; Meg. 29ᵇ שואלין בהלכות וכ׳; Y. Pes. I, 27ᵇ bot.; Bab.
units: <cite ref="Pesachim 6a">Pes. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>שואלין בהלכות וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>שואלין ודורשין</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note); <cite ref="Sanhedrin 12b">Snh. 12ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: (cmp. בְּעֵי I) to beg to remark, to submit.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 1:1:5">Y. Shek. I, beg. 45ᵈ</cite> <he>ר׳ חזקיה ש׳ מעתה וכ׳</he> R. Ḥ. remarked, according to this &c. Ib. 46ᵇ.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 9:3:4">Y. Snh. IX, 27ᵃ</cite> bot.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to ask for a loan, to borrow.
units: Sabb. XXIII, 1 שואל אדם מחבירו וכ׳ a man may borrow of his neighbor vessels of wine or oil (on the Sabbath), but must not say הַלְוֵינִי (v. infra Hif.); a. fr.—Esp. to borrow an object for use (with ref. to Ex. XXII, 13 sq.).

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 103a:5">B. Mets. 103ᵃ</cite> <he>שואל אדם בטובו לעולם</he> if a person borrows an object (saying, ‘lend it to me) for its usefulness’, it is a standing loan (he is permitted to take it whenever he desires to use it).
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 8:1">Ib. VIII, 1</cite> <he>השואל את הפרה וש׳ בעליה עמה</he> if a person borrows a cow for work, borrowing her owner with her (the owner lending his personal service).
Ib. 95ᵇ שָׁאֲלָהּ ואחר כך ש׳ וכ׳ if he borrowed the cow only, and after a while borrowed her owner; a. fr.—שׁוֹאֵל the borrower of an object.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 95a:11">Ib. 95ᵃ</cite> <he>חיובא דש׳</he> the responsibility of the borrower.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 96b:1">Ib. 96ᵇ</cite> top <he>ש׳ הוי או שוכר הוי</he> is he legally considered a borrower or a hirer? <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 3:2">Ib. III, 2</cite> <he>והש׳ ישלם וכ׳</he> and the borrower must indemnify the hirer; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Shabbat 96b:9-12">Sabb. 96ᵇ</cite> <he>אורגי … לשׁוֹאֲלֵיהֶן</he> (Ar. <he>לשווליהן</he>, v. <cite ref="U00352"><he>שְׁוַולְיָא</he></cite>) the curtain weavers were wont to throw the clue over to such as would borrow it from them.—Part. pass. <cite ref="U00012"><he>שָׁאוּל</he></cite>; f. <cite ref="U00015"><he>שְׁאוּלָה</he></cite> &c.

<cite ref="Taanit 23b:3">Taan. 23ᵇ</cite> <he>טלית ש׳ היתה וכ׳</he> it was a cloak that had been lent to me, I had borrowed it for such a purpose (for ordinary wear), but not for that purpose (to wear it when carrying a load).

<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 4:8">Ib. IV, 8</cite> <he>שבחן … בכלי לבן שְׁאוּלִין וכ׳</he> on those days the maidens of Zion went out (to the vineyards) in white garments borrowed for the purpose, in order not to put to shame those who had none; a. fr.— [<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 65">Gen. R. s. 65</cite> <he>לא שאול … ולא שאולה</he>, v. next w.—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 19">Gen. R. s. 19</cite> <he>שאולת חומץ</he>, read: <he>שׁוֹאֶלֶת</he>, a woman asking for some vinegar.]
<cite ref="Berakhot 6b:2">Ber. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>כל הרגיל … הקב״ה מַשְׁאִיל בו</he> if one who comes regularly to synagogue fails to come one day, the Lord holds inquiry about him.
<cite ref="Yevamot 76b:14">Yeb. 76ᵇ</cite> <he>עד שאתה משאיל עליו … שְׁאַל וכ׳</he> instead of inquiring about him whether or not he is fit for government, ask whether &c.
<cite ref="Yevamot 76b:11">Ib.</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>אאבוה קא משאיל</he> he (Saul) asked (Abner) to inquire who his (David’s) father was.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 123a:16">B. Bath. 123ᵃ</cite> <he>היתה יושבת … ומַשְׁאֶלֶת וכ׳</he> she sat at the cross-roads and made inquiries; a. e.
<cite ref="Shabbat 148a:6">Sabb. 148ᵃ</cite> (ref. to Mish.

ib. XIII, 1, v. supra) מאי שנא הַשְׁאִילֵינִי ומאי שנא הלויני what is the difference, whether you say hashileni (lend me) or halveni (loan me)? השאיליני לא אתי למיכתב וכ׳ when you say ‘lend me’, no document is expected to be written for it &c.

<cite ref="Mishnah Nedarim 4:6">Ned. IV, 6</cite> <he>חמודר … לא יַשְׁאִילֶנּוּ ולא יִשְׁאַל ממנו</he> he who by his neighbor’s vow is forbidden any benefit at his hand, must neither lend him nor borrow from him &c.
B. Mets. 116ᵃ דברים העשויין להַשְׁאִיל וכ׳ things which are frequently lent out or hired out; a. fr.—מַשְׁאִיל the lender, owner of the lent object.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 96a:12">Ib. 96ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—[Pesik. Vayhi, p. 63ᵃ <he>שאילו השאיל</he>, v. <cite ref="U00661"><he>שָׁחַל</he> II</cite>.]
<cite ref="Yoma 73a:19">Yoma 73ᵃ</cite> <he>בגדים … נ׳ בהן</he> when the war chaplain is consulted, he wears the garments which the high priest wears when he officiates, v. supra.
<cite ref="Yoma 85a:13">Ib. 85ᵃ</cite> <he>נִשְׁאֲלָח שאלה וכ׳</he> the following question was asked in their presence; <cite ref="Kiddushin 40b">Kidd. 40ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Nedarim 81a">Ned. 81ᵃ</cite> <he>דבר זה נ׳ לחכמים וכ׳</he> this problem was placed before the scholars and the prophets, and they could not solve it &c.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: נ׳ על to allow one’s self to be asked about the circumstances of a case, to appear before a scholar for a decision on a ritual case. Y. Ter. VIII, 46ᵃ bot. שדעתו להִישָּׁאֵל עליה a case (of T’rumah) which he had intended to have a scholar decide.
units: <cite ref="Yoma 2a">Ib.</cite> <he>הריני מניחה על מנת שאֶישָּׁאֵל עליה</he> I put it (the doubtful T’rumah) aside with the intention of having it decided &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Tahorot 3:6">Toh. III, 6</cite> <he>שאין בו דעת להִשָּׁאֵל</he> (a child) whose mind is not sufficiently developed to be questioned.
Ib. V, 5 אם נִשְׁאֲלוּ זה וכ׳ if they come for a decision, each of them separately; a. fr.—Esp. (על נדרו) נ׳ to come before a scholar for absolution from a vow.

<cite ref="Nedarim 90a:4">Ned. 90ᵃ</cite> <he>קונם … ולמי שאֶשָּׁאֵל עליו</he> if one vows, I will not be benefited by N. N., nor by any scholar to whom I may apply for absolution from this vow; <he>נ׳ על הראשון וכ׳</he> he must first apply for absolution from the first part of the vow, and then from the second.

<cite ref="Nedarim 90a:4">Ib.</cite> <he>נ׳ על נדרו … נזרו</he> he must first apply for absolution from his vow of abstinence, and then from his nazaritic vow. Ib. 69ᵃ <he>נִשְׁאָלִין על ההקם וכ׳</he> you may apply for absolution in order to revoke your confirmation (of your daughter’s vow), but you cannot do so in order to revoke your invalidation; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be borrowed, to do gratuitous service.
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 96a:14">B. Mets. 96ᵃ</cite> <he>שותפין ששאלו ונ׳ לאחד מהן</he> if partners borrow an animal for work, and its owner lends his services to one of them individually.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 96a:16">Ib.</cite> <he>האומר לשלוחו צא והִשָּׁאֵל לי וכ׳</he> (not <he>והשאיל</he>) if a person says to his deputy, go out and do work in my behalf together with my cow (lent to my neighbor).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 96a:21">Ib.</cite> <he>האומר לעבדו צא והשאל עם וכ׳</he> if he says to his slave, go out and do work &c.; a. e.
